body:
## What to build

`is_name_only_expr()` answers whether tidyselect settles an expression from the
column names alone. #342 established that question and closed the three shapes
it named. Two shapes still answer `FALSE` that the question settles as `TRUE`,
and neither is reachable by the edit #342 made — each is held out by a decision
that lives somewhere else.

### 1. `~`, which the reader cannot see

tidyselect refuses a formula in a selection outright, in `stop_formula()`, so
its failure depends on nothing and a fortiori not on column types. Measured
against `grouping_selection_proxy()`:

```
grouping_set(~c(region))   reads=1   Formula shorthand must be wrapped in `where()`.
.by = ~c(region)           reads=1   Formula shorthand must be wrapped in `where()`.
```

That is the ordering ADR 0005 forbids, and it is the same defect #342 fixed for
`*`, `^`, `&&`, and `||`. Adding `"~"` to `selection_refused_operators()` does
not reach it: `is_nameable_call()` declines a call to `~`, so
`static_call_name()` answers `NULL` and `is_name_only_expr()` returns `FALSE`
before any operator set is consulted. That refusal is deliberate and has its
own reasons (ADR 0019, #163, and the formula tests in
`tests/testthat/test-static-expression-analysis.R`), so this needs a reading
that does not route through the name, not a wider list.

### 2. `.data$x`, which the reader declines conservatively

`.data$region` is a valid selection settled by the names — tidyselect's walk
has a `.data` branch of its own — and it currently costs a snapshot:

```
grouping_set(.data$region)   reads=1   (succeeds)
```

No error is deferred, so this is not an ADR 0005 violation; the fast pass is
skipped where the names would have settled the plan. It is narrower than it
looks: `.data$x` with a literal name is settled, while `.data[[var]]` is not,
so whatever reads this has to tell a symbol right-hand side from an expression
one. `.data$x` is also deprecated in a tidyselect selection, which is a reason
to weigh before spending anything on it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `.grouping` or `.by` selection written as a formula raises before any
      query reaches the backend, for both arguments, without widening what
      `is_nameable_call()` names.
- [ ] `.data$x` is either settled by names or deliberately left `FALSE` with
      the reason recorded at the site. Answering "left alone" is a valid close;
      answering it by silence is not.
- [ ] Whatever reads `.data$` distinguishes a literal name from `.data[[var]]`,
      or does not claim to read `.data` at all.
- [ ] The read count is what a test asserts, as
      `tests/testthat/test-grouping-plan.R`'s ordering block already does.

## Context

#342 and PR #345 establish the invariant, the two readers' relationship, and
the read-counting test these would extend. `d159b9b`'s
`selection_refused_operators()` is the set item 1 would join if it could.

title: Settle the two selection shapes the name-only reader still cannot reach
